basic_info.name: Fleury (Grupo Fleury / Fleury Medicina e Saude). Patient-facing surfaces: 'Fleury' app (Fleury Pacientes), results portals (resultados.fleury.com.br, resultados.grupofleury.com.br), 'Grupo Fleury Saude Digital' app, Saude iD, Cuidar Digital, Fleury em Casa, Fleury Genomica.
basic_info.category: Diagnostic medicine conglomerate (clinical analysis, diagnostic imaging, pathological anatomy, genomics) with a transactional patient app — not an interpreter. B2B lab operations for hospitals.
basic_info.stage: Public (B3: FLRY3). Founded 1926 (centenary in 2026, campaign 'O futuro ja tem 100 anos'). Merged with Hermes Pardini in 2023; still acquiring (GIP Medicina Diagnostica, ~R$207.5M, approved by CADE without restrictions in 2026). Growing, profitable, consolidating.
basic_info.pricing_model: No consumer subscription. Pay-per-exam for self-payers (particular), billing via health insurers (convenios), and B2B contracts (~40 partner hospitals plus third-party lab processing, which is 55.5% of exam volume). App and results access free. Paid add-ons: telemedicine consultations (Pronto Atendimento Digital, Cuidar Digital), home collection (Fleury em Casa), genetic panels (Fleury Genomica), checkup packages, vaccines. Smiles miles redemption partnership (Saude iD). Exact price tables not published online; quoted at units/booking. [uncertain: exact current price points]
basic_info.target_user: Premium/ABC1 insured patients (core Fleury brand), price-sensitive and uninsured via Saude iD, corporate/employer clients (B2B2C, incl. mental health digital programs), hospitals and third-party labs (B2B), and ordering physicians (doctor portal).
basic_info.scale_metrics: ~540-585 units across 13-14 states [uncertain: exact count varies by source]; ~368 million exams/year (some sources ~330M) = ~40 million tests/month incl. clinical analysis, imaging, pathology, genomics; 5,000+ doctors; 6M+ patients/year. FY2025: revenue ~R$9B, EBITDA ~R$2.1B, net profit ~R$612M; Q2 2026 net profit R$221.8M. Most valuable laboratory brand in Brazil (~R$1.42B brand value). iOS app 4.9 stars / ~17k ratings. Durable threat assessment: as a diagnostics OPERATOR they are a fortress (scale, brand, automation), but their patient app is transactional — not competing for the interpretation layer today.

product.core_features: Exam results access (fast, with PDF download/share/print), end-to-end exam tracking from collection to release with release-date prediction and result filters, online scheduling (exams, vaccines, consults), exam preparation instructions, unit map, digital vaccination record (carteira de vacinacao), multi-profile management (dependents) in one app, results summary view plus images/videos of imaging exams, evolutionary tables and graphs (app v4.6.0), notification/journey area (v3.5.0), authorization status tracking (v3.6.0), WhatsApp service channel (results in PDF, scheduling, cancellation), telemedicine (Pronto Atendimento Digital, Cuidar Digital), home collection (Fleury em Casa), genetic testing without scheduling/fasting (Fleury Genomica).
product.signature_differentiator: Vertically integrated diagnostics trust machine: they PRODUCE the exams (own labs, imaging, pathology, genomics) so results arrive natively in-app with zero upload friction; 85% of exams auto-released with no human intervention (up to 92-98% in some areas); CAP ISO 15189 accredited — first and only lab in Latin America, one of ~65 worldwide; 100-year premium brand. Nobody else in Brazil combines this operational automation with premium brand equity. But note: the differentiator is back-office excellence, not patient-facing intelligence.
product.lab_data_handling: Own-lab vertical: results flow automatically from their own analyzers/radiology into the app — no PDF upload, no external lab ingestion, no cross-lab unified history. Interpretation is NOT offered to patients: laudo stays technical; doubts are routed to the ordering physician (Chat Medico on the doctor portal is doctor-to-Fleury-lab, not patient-facing). Retest cadence driven by physician orders, not product-driven nudges. Hardware footprint: physical units + Fleury em Casa home collection; no wearables/CGM/at-home chips — blood drawn at their network. Genomics (Fleury Genomica + Genesis Genomics JV with Hospital Einstein) sells hereditary panels direct-to-consumer-ish (no scheduling/fasting) but as paid tests, not as an integrated longitudinal layer.
product.family_dependents_depth: Multi-profile in one app: 'total control over your health and that of your dependents' — results and vaccination wallet for children/spouse. Beyond that, shallow: no pediatric reference-range presentation, no caregiver mode, no family-level hereditary risk engine tying Fleury Genomica results to relatives' lab trends. Family story is account management, not family health intelligence. [uncertain: depth of pediatric views and caregiver controls not publicly documented]
product.doctor_sharing: Patient side: share/download/print PDF results — classic document handoff, no structured brief. Doctor side: Portal Medico (resultados.fleury.com.br/medico) with exam results, online image viewer, and Chat Medico (physician clarifies laudo doubts directly with Fleury's lab team). No consultation-brief/SOAP export, no pre-visit summary, no doctor-facing dashboard of patient trends beyond the results viewer. The doctor relationship is 'Fleury serves the ordering physician', not 'patient prepares the visit'.
product.action_loop_monetization: Closed internal loop, margin captured in-house: result in app -> (if alarmed) telemedicine consult via Pronto Atendimento Digital / Cuidar Digital -> new exams ordered land back in Fleury's own labs. Upsells: checkup packages, vaccines, Fleury em Casa convenience, Fleury Genomica panels, Saude iD membership-ish digital care for the uninsured, corporate mental-health programs, Smiles miles redemption. No supplements marketplace, no third-party marketplace, no protocol sales — monetization is 'own the next exam and the consult', classic vertical capture. For Dr. Exame: their action loop is deep but closed to their own network; nothing for patients whose follow-up lies outside Fleury.

technology.ai_approach: Operational/back-office AI, explicitly not patient-facing: 85% of exams released without human intervention (some areas 92%, 95%, 98%) — and leadership stresses this automation predates modern AI (fuzzy logic, boolean logic: 'fast, effective, low-cost'). Image recognition + automated cell classification raised hematology productivity 3-4x; AI in cytogenetics to offset specialist scarcity; AI in MRI equipment halved acquisition time (double throughput on same scanner); AI triage of CT scans prioritizes serious cases (~1,500 serious cases flagged). Partnerships over the years: Kunumi (COVID imaging), IBM Watson-era omnichannel virtual assistant, DataH (pneumonia detection). Public philosophy (Gustavo Stuani, Ops & B2B director, Forum Saude Digital 2026): 'random data serves nothing', they rejected AI where 'gain was so marginal and cost so much higher it made no sense'. No LLM, no patient-facing interpretation engine, no consumer AI claims. 15% of exams still get human physician review.
technology.data_inputs: Own diagnostic output only: clinical analysis, imaging, pathological anatomy, genomics; plus vaccination records and scheduling/process telemetry (they mine operational data: request->collection->tube->release->critical-result times, ~40M tests/month). No wearable, CGM, questionnaire-based intake, or external lab ingestion publicly offered. [uncertain: internal wearable/monitor pilots not verifiable]
technology.data_interoperability: Patient exhaust: PDF download/share/print, WhatsApp PDF delivery, web portals. Professional: Portal Medico with image viewer. B2B: integrations with ~40 hospitals (clinical analysis, imaging, pathology) and third-party lab processing (55.5% of volume). NOT found: FHIR, RNDS connectivity, Apple Health Records, Android Health Connect, public/open API for patients, or any external-PDF ingestion. Ecosystem is deliberately closed — data enters through their needles and scanners and exits as PDF/portal views. [uncertain: absence of public evidence; internal HL7/FHIR with hospital partners is likely but undocumented]
technology.platform: iOS + Android consumer apps ('Fleury' / Fleury Pacientes; separate 'Grupo Fleury Saude Digital' app), web portals (resultados.fleury.com.br, resultados.grupofleury.com.br), WhatsApp channel (11 3179-0822), doctor web portal, B2B lab services. No public developer API.

ux.onboarding: Two doors: results portal with ID + password printed on the exam card (legacy, still live), or app account. Time-to-value is near-zero for an existing Fleury patient: result appears the moment it is released, with predicted release date shown while pending. For non-patients the app is a scheduling kiosk. No interpretation onboarding — first value is 'see your number', not 'understand your number'.
ux.data_visualization: App v4.6.0 added 'images, videos and a summary of exam results, plus tables and graphs with an evolutionary view' — trend tables/graphs over time and evolving reports (laudo evolutivo) for comparison across dates. Reference-range flagging exists inside laudos (standard lab formatting). No composite health score, no severity-aware lay summaries, no 'what changed since last exam' narrative, no biological-age/risk scores. Visualization = faithful rendering of lab data, not translation. [uncertain: exact chart types/flag styling in-app]
ux.engagement_channel: Deeply transactional: open-on-result then churn. Mechanics: push notifications for exam journey (v3.5.0 notification area), release predictions, scheduling reminders; WhatsApp as a SERVICE channel (schedule, cancel, fetch PDF) not a retention channel; heavy Instagram marketing for app novelties. No community, no streaks, no proactive health programs for consumers, no nudges to retest. Retention is structural, not product-driven: patients return when a physician orders exams or when their convenio routes them back. The 6M+ patients/year flow is owned by the lab funnel, not by engagement design.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Strongest-in-class ops credibility: CAP ISO 15189 accreditation (first and only in Latin America, ~65 labs worldwide), ANVISA-licensed operations, 100-year brand, 15% of exams still physician-reviewed, hospital-grade critical-result workflows. But: no published accuracy claims or methodology for anything patient-facing (there are no patient-facing AI claims to validate); app features ship without published validation; automation stats (85%) come from executive talks, not audited papers. Billing transparency is standard Brazilian lab practice (convenio tables / unit quotes), not itemized in-app education. Risks: trust is concentrated in the laudo/physician chain — the patient-facing layer inherits trust without adding transparency.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Classic provider posture: regulated as diagnostic medicine services (ANVISA licensing, health accreditations) — their AI lives inside vendor equipment (MRI/CT) and internal lab processes, so patient-facing SaMD rules (ANVISA RDC 657/2022) barely touch them; they make no diagnostic AI claims to consumers, hence no disclaimers needed and no regulatory ceiling hit. LGPD: standard compliance posture, no major breach found in searches. Interpretation liability is structurally outsourced: 'ask your ordering physician' is the wall. For Dr. Exame this confirms the ceiling is navigable: Fleury's own behavior shows you can be Brazil's most trusted diagnostics brand while routing all interpretation through physicians.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: GAPS (Dr. Exame openings): (1) No patient-facing interpretation — Chat Medico is doctor-only; patients with laudo doubts are told to call their physician; the summary view shows data, not meaning. (2) Closed ecosystem — only Fleury-produced exams; no PDF upload, no cross-lab unification (every Brazilian who mixes Fleury/Dasa/Hermes Pardini-legacy exams has no home). (3) No family/hereditary intelligence — multi-profile is account management; genomics panels sold à la carte, not woven into relatives' trends. (4) No retest cadence, no 'what changed', no questions-for-your-doctor brief. (5) WhatsApp used for service, not retention. (6) No engagement between exams — transactional churn by design. WHAT WORKS (inspiration, not copy): release-date prediction + start-to-finish tracking (kills result anxiety loop — steal this); evolutionary graphs/tables in-app; multi-profile dependents with vaccination wallet; WhatsApp PDF delivery; 85% auto-release as the operational benchmark; 'not everything needs AI' cost discipline; CAP ISO 15189 as the trust artifact to emulate with equivalent clinical-governance signaling.
trust_gaps.relevance: HIGH. Largest premium diagnostics player in Brazil, source-of-truth for ~368M exams/year, and the brand patients trust most in labs. They own the upstream of Dr. Exame's pipeline (patients hold Fleury PDFs) and represent both the moat (they could bolt on interpretation overnight and reach millions instantly) and the validation (even they have NOT built patient-facing interpretation — the gap is real and durable because their business model monetizes the next exam, not understanding). Dr. Exame's complements-not-competes posture toward Fleury is correct: ingest their PDFs, add the meaning layer they refuse to build.
